decisive_items: Severe emphysema and bullous changes throughout the lungs
Marked hyperinflated lungs with coarse interstitial thickening and scarring
response.rationale: R7 best integrates the smoking history, severe emphysema/bullous morphology, and hyperinflation/scarring seen on CT. Pneumothorax-only candidates rely on a single acute finding and do not explain the underlying chronic lung disease; substance-induced labels are not directly supported by raw spans. R1 is a strong narrower emphysema descriptor, but R7 accounts for the additional hyperinflation/scarring and is the more complete syndrome.

rejected.why: Restatement of R5 with anatomy modifier; substance-induced cause is not raw-supported.

Correlated append-only restatement of R7; adds no new raw evidence beyond the parent candidate.
Substance-induced pneumothorax lacks raw support for causation and ignores severe emphysema/bullous disease.
Bullous lung disease is descriptive and omits the smoking history and hyperinflation supporting COPD.
Only a urine drug screen is cited; no raw support for respiratory depression as the diagnosis and it misses the lung imaging findings.
Spontaneous pneumothorax is an acute complication without addressing the underlying severe emphysema/bullous changes or smoking cause.
Restatement of R6 with misleading left-lower-lung localization; the actual findings are diffuse and left-greater-than-right.
